status: Bounded assistant source-based review of five selected cases; not a census or independent ground truth

cases.name: Roe v. Wade

components.issue: Protection against a life-saving-only abortion ban
components.decision: Invalidated the Texas prohibition and recognized constitutional protection subject to pregnancy-stage limits.
components.scope: Protection was not unlimited at every pregnancy stage.
components.survey_fit: General permission categories supply context; they do not ask about constitutional protection or the stage-dependent framework.

cases.interpretation_limit: Historical holding, later overruled. Broad permission is not approval of the full Roe framework.

cases.name: Harris v. McRae

components.issue: Public financing of medically necessary abortions
components.decision: Upheld Hyde funding restrictions; Medicaid participation did not require states to fund abortions excluded from federal reimbursement.
components.scope: Public subsidy obligations, distinct from permission to obtain an abortion.
components.locator: Opinion Parts II and III; syllabus holdings 1 and 2.
components.survey_fit: No funding-specific observation is included. General legality and abortion in cases of poverty do not measure public-financing preferences.

cases.interpretation_limit: Direct denotes the policy a suitable question would need to address; none is matched. No funding agreement is inferred.

cases.name: Planned Parenthood v. Casey

components.decision: Retained Roe’s essential protection while replacing its trimester framework with the undue-burden standard.
components.scope: Core protection retained; regulatory doctrine changed.
components.locator: Joint opinion Parts I and IV.
components.survey_fit: General abortion preferences are context, not a referendum on this legal standard.

components.scope: Married women subject to the challenged provision.
components.survey_fit: No selected question directly asks about spousal notification.

components.decision: Allowed the challenged informed-consent and 24-hour waiting requirements.
components.scope: Facial challenge to these provisions; not approval of every possible waiting rule.
components.survey_fit: No selected question directly asks about these requirements.

components.decision: Allowed one-parent consent with judicial bypass.
components.survey_fit: No selected question measures this particular consent-and-bypass rule.

cases.interpretation_limit: Mixed selected components, not one signed score. This is not exhaustive: reporting and emergency provisions are not separately analyzed. Votes differ by part.

cases.name: Whole Woman’s Health v. Hellerstedt

components.decision: Invalidated Texas admitting-privileges and surgical-center requirements.
components.scope: Removed the challenged provider barriers, not all abortion regulation.
components.locator: Breyer opinion introduction and Parts IV–V.
components.survey_fit: General legality supplies context only; no selected question specifically measures either provider requirement.

cases.interpretation_limit: Historical ruling under the then-applicable standard. General support does not establish agreement with the medical-benefit assessment.

cases.name: Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization

components.decision: Removed federal constitutional abortion protection by overruling Roe and Casey.
components.scope: Removal of federal protection, not enactment of a nationwide abortion ban.
components.survey_fit: VOTER explicitly asks whether Roe should be overturned. Support is oriented toward retaining Roe. This matches that named component, not every aspect of Dobbs.

components.decision: Reversed the judgment blocking Mississippi’s law under the prior constitutional standard.
components.scope: Fifteen-week rule with specified exceptions; distinct from the separate overruling component.
components.locator: Majority Part VI; syllabus description of the law.
components.survey_fit: No selected question asks about this fifteen-week rule with its exceptions.

cases.interpretation_limit: Five justices joined overruling Roe/Casey; Roberts concurred in the judgment without endorsing that step. The judgment’s 6–3 split must not be assigned to every component.
